title: Festivals & Culture
description: Survive Chinese New Year visiting, getai season and everything in between.

example.zh: 农历新年 我们 回 外婆 家。
example.en: We go to Grandma's for Chinese New Year.

example.zh: 今年 收到 很 多 红包。
example.en: Got lots of red packets this year.

example.zh: 初一 去 亲戚 家 拜年。
example.en: On the first day we visit relatives.

example.zh: 年夜饭 全家 一起 吃。
example.en: The whole family has reunion dinner together.

example.zh: 恭喜发财， 红包 拿 来！
example.en: Gong xi fa cai — hand over the red packet!

items.note: Bring two when visiting at CNY — 柑 sounds like 金 (gold) in Cantonese and Hokkien.

example.zh: 拜年 要 带 两个 柑。
example.en: Bring two oranges when visiting.

items.note: Tossing the raw-fish salad as high as you can for good luck.

example.zh: 大家 一起 捞鱼生！
example.en: Everyone toss the yusheng together!

items.note: Sounds like 年高 — "higher every year".

example.zh: 奶奶 自己 做 年糕。
example.en: Grandma makes her own nian gao.

items.note: Singapore and Malaysia say 黄梨; in China it's 菠萝. Pineapple tarts (黄梨挞) are the CNY must-have — and 黄梨 sounds like "fortune comes" in Hokkien (ong lai).

example.zh: 黄梨挞 一 下子 就 吃 完 了。
example.en: The pineapple tarts were gone in no time.

example.zh: 商场 有 舞狮 表演。
example.en: There's a lion dance at the mall.

example.zh: 新加坡 不 可以 随便 放 鞭炮。
example.en: You can't just set off firecrackers in Singapore.

example.zh: 过年 就是 要 团圆。
example.en: New Year is all about being together.

example.zh: 中秋节 吃 月饼。
example.en: We eat mooncakes at Mid-Autumn.

example.zh: 我 喜欢 冰皮 月饼。
example.en: I like snowskin mooncakes.

example.zh: 小孩 提 着 灯笼 玩。
example.en: The kids are playing with lanterns.

example.zh: 端午节 有 龙舟 比赛。
example.en: There are dragon boat races at Duanwu.

example.zh: 外婆 包 的 粽子 最 好吃。
example.en: Grandma's rice dumplings are the best.

example.zh: 清明节 我们 去 拜祭 祖先。
example.en: At Qing Ming we pay respects to our ancestors.

example.zh: 中元节 晚上 不 要 乱 走。
example.en: Don't wander around at night during Hungry Ghost month.

items.note: Loud, glittery stage shows during the seventh lunar month — the front row is left empty for the spirits.

example.zh: 组屋 楼下 有 歌台。
example.en: There's a getai at the void deck.

example.zh: 国庆日 有 烟花。
example.en: There are fireworks on National Day.

example.zh: 屠妖节 的 小印度 很 漂亮。
example.en: Little India is beautiful at Deepavali.

example.zh: 开斋节 去 芽笼 看 灯饰。
example.en: Go to Geylang to see the lights for Hari Raya.

example.zh: 圣诞节 快乐！
example.en: Merry Christmas!

items.note: Also the casual way to say "bye-bye"!

example.zh: 初一 十五 去 庙 拜拜。
example.en: Go pray at the temple on the 1st and 15th.

example.zh: 奶奶 每天 烧香。
example.en: Grandma burns incense every day.

example.zh: 这 间 庙 有 一百 年 历史。
example.en: This temple is a hundred years old.

example.zh: 八 是 吉利 的 数字。
example.en: Eight is a lucky number.

items.note: Never gift a clock (送钟 sounds like 送终, attending a deathbed).

example.zh: 送礼 不 要 送 钟。
example.en: Never give a clock as a gift.

example.zh: 谢谢 你 的 祝福。
example.en: Thank you for your good wishes.

example.zh: 祝 你 新年快乐！
example.en: Happy New Year to you!

example.zh: 妈妈， 生日快乐！
example.en: Happy birthday, Mum!

example.zh: 祝 外婆 身体健康！
example.en: Wishing Grandma good health!

example.zh: 新年 快乐， 万事如意！
example.en: Happy New Year, may all go well!

example.zh: 祝 大家 中秋快乐！
example.en: Happy Mid-Autumn, everyone!

example.zh: 恭喜 你 找到 新 工作！
example.en: Congrats on the new job!
